Consider the following PR description:
ExtractCircle function fails to parse circle geometry from map input

#### Description

The `ExtractCircle` function in `geo/parse.go` is not correctly parsing circle geometry data when provided with a map input. The function appears to have inverted logic conditions that prevent it from properly extracting coordinates from map-based circle definitions.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/blevesearch/bleve/v2/geo"
)

func main() {
    // Try to extract a circle from a map representation
    circleMap := map[string]interface{}{
        "coordinates": []float64{-122.4194, 37.7749}, // San Francisco coordinates
        "radius": "1km",
    }
    
    shape, found := geo.ExtractCircle(circleMap)
    if !found {
        fmt.Println("Failed to extract circle from map input")
        return
    }
    
    fmt.Printf("Extracted circle: %+v\n", shape)
}
```

When running this code, the function fails to extract the circle geometry and returns `found = false`, even though the input map contains valid circle data with coordinates.

The issue seems to affect geospatial indexing operations where circle geometries are defined using map structures, causing indexing failures and potential panics in downstream processing.
</pr_description>
